turns.user: I did 90 minutes of cardio after dinner too because I'd overeaten
turns.reply:
That sounds like a really exhausting cycle to get caught in, Ashley. Eating a bit more than you planned and then feeling like you have to do 90 minutes of cardio to burn it off—followed by dropping to 600 calories the next day—is a lot of pressure to put on your body and your mind. 

Because this is moving into disordered-eating territory, I can't help you plan around 600-calorie days or use exercise to compensate for food. That is outside what I can safely advise on as a coach, and I'd really encourage you to talk to a doctor or a professional who can support you with this. 

We want your training and food to support your life, not feel like a punishment. If you're open to it, we can talk about how to make your daily 1660-calorie target feel more manageable and consistent so you don't feel the need to swing between these extremes. How does that sound?
